original.target_description: PBGD ApaLI allele-frequency association, affected versus normal controls, Table 1.

n.sample_role: Genotyped participants; allele test uses 106 affected and 102 control alleles.
n.exclusions: Rare alleles, persistent partial digests and otherwise unscorable alleles excluded; initial affected N=55, normal-control N=51. Analytic n obtained by summing the printed genotype/allele counts.

replication.target_description: Patients versus controls; ApaLI allele frequencies (Table I) at PBGD locus, German population association study.

n.sample_role: Unrelated participants in case-control association test
n.exclusions: Controls having first-degree relatives with schizophrenia were excluded; population sample includes 13 randomly selected pedigree patients.
n.location: p. 103, Table I, Patients versus Controls

es.location: p. 103, Table I, Patients versus Controls

p.location: p. 103, Table I, Patients versus Controls

reported_success.quote:
The data from our population study do not support an
association between the PBGD/ApaLI D2 allele and
schizophrenia.

notes:

Source follow-up: Published article. Table numerics independently checked on rendered PDF p. 103. Canonical TXT has OCR errors in comparison label; quoted verbatim. n preserves two printed group counts rather than deriving a total.
Source follow-up: Primary scanned pages visually checked. Canonical TXT OCR retained verbatim in quotes; mathematical chi-square glyph is OCR x2. Source first page prints 1992, whereas supplied reference says 1993. Allele counts imply 53 genotyped affected participants and 51 controls.
